definitions.gloss: revision, amendment (of a text, document, or publication)
definitions.explanation: The act of correcting, updating, or improving the content of a written work such as a book, textbook, dictionary, or manual. Focuses on textual content rather than legal or institutional rules.

examples.japanese: {教科書|きょうかしょ}を{改訂|かいてい}する。
{改訂|かいてい}{版|ばん}が{来月|らいげつ}{出版|しゅっぱん}される。
examples.english: The revised edition will be published next month.

examples.japanese: この{辞書|じしょ}は{十|じゅう}{年|ねん}ぶりに{大幅|おおはば}に{改訂|かいてい}され、{新語|しんご}が{多数|たすう}{追加|ついか}された。
examples.english: This dictionary underwent a major revision for the first time in ten years, with many new words added.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
{改訂|かいてい} vs. {改定|かいてい}: Both are read かいてい but have different scopes. {改訂|かいてい} (with {訂|てい} meaning "correct") refers to revising the content of texts, books, and documents. {改定|かいてい} (with {定|てい} meaning "fix, establish") refers to changing rules, standards, prices, or regulations. For example, a textbook is {改訂|かいてい}される while a price is {改定|かいてい}される.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {改訂|かいてい}{版|ばん}: revised edition
- {大幅|おおはば}に{改訂|かいてい}する: to revise extensively
- {改訂|かいてい}{作業|さぎょう}: revision work
- {全面|ぜんめん}{改訂|かいてい}: complete revision

cross_references.description: changing rules, standards, or prices (not textual content)
